description: Write a pandas ETL script for adtech_platform that removes accidental duplicate click events. Two clicks by the same user on the same ad are duplicates when the later one occurs less than 5 seconds after the previous kept click. The script should: (1) parse click_ts to UTC, (2) sort by user_id, ad_id, click_ts, (3) iterate within each (user_id, ad_id) group keeping a click only if it is at least 5 seconds after the last kept click, (4) output the kept clicks and a count of removed duplicates per group.
edge_cases: k3 is 3 seconds after the removed k2 but 6 seconds after the last kept click k1, so it is kept; comparing each row to its immediate predecessor (diff/lag) would wrongly drop it
k4 is exactly 5 seconds after k3: the rule is strict (< 5 s is a duplicate), so it is kept
k5 belongs to another user and is unaffected even though it is within 5 seconds of k1
common_failure_modes: FM3: Lag-based comparison against the previous row instead of the previous kept row removes chains of valid clicks
FM2: Off-by-one on the 5-second boundary (<= instead of <)
FM1: Window partition missing ad_id or user_id dedups across unrelated users
